items.excerpt: Nobel laureate Giorgio Parisi and Francesco Zamponi used Anthropic's Claude to crack a decade-old problem in jamming physics, proving why two parameters always sum to 1. The team reached a publishable proof in roughly 40 prompts, shifting their view of what LLMs can contribute to theoretical physics.

Researchers used AI to design synthetic RNA-guided nucleases with properties not found in nature, matching or exceeding the activity of natural CRISPR enzymes in cells. The Science paper lays out a strategy for generating non-natural genome-editing proteins from scratch.

OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol resolved the cycle double cover conjecture, open for more than 50 years. The account details the prompting scaffolding — parallel agents, persistent nudging — that turned a chatbot into a working proof collaborator.

Neural networks trained to spot biosignatures can be fooled into confidently misclassifying molecules that fall outside their training distribution. Researchers drove false-positive rates to 100% with as few as 150 modifications, arguing for human verification in life-detection missions.

DGIST researchers built an artificial olfactory system pairing metal-organic frameworks with AI that can discriminate tens of thousands of distinct odors. It mimics human smell via combinatorial coding across sensors, with uses from disease diagnosis to environmental monitoring.

Clarkson University unveiled KANDy, an AI system that recovers the governing equations of complex, chaotic systems directly from data. Unlike black-box predictors, it returns interpretable symbolic dynamics alongside its forecasts.

Keio University researchers used a machine-learning framework called FMQA with an Ising machine to design RNA sequences that fold into target structures. The study finds the encoding strategy is decisive to how well AI and quantum-inspired optimizers perform.

Computer scientist Peter J. Denning argues AI has been built on a flawed assumption traceable to Turing's 1950 paper. His claim: machines cannot encode tacit knowledge — common sense, embodied skill — so human-level AI stays out of reach.

University of Illinois researchers found the brain begins deciding earlier than assumed, with primary sensory regions participating through feedback loops. The team frames it as a lesson for AI: feedforward CNN-style architectures may be missing a cheaper, biologically grounded design.

An AI+RES framework couples machine learning emulators with rare-event sampling to estimate how often extreme heatwaves occur. It matches conventional climate simulations while using up to 1,000x less compute, making rare-event statistics tractable.

A Physics World episode on 'large physics models' — AI systems trained on physics rather than text — applied to vehicle aerodynamics. David Wheater explains blending computational fluid dynamics with wind-tunnel data to build surrogate models.

University of Washington researchers designed AI-generated protein sheaths ('Wraps') that solubilise membrane proteins while preserving their structure and function. The sequences are genetically encoded and co-expressed with the target protein in E. coli.
Anthropic unveiled Claude Science, an AI application aimed at biopharma research labs. The piece frames it as a test of whether AI in the lab advances discovery rather than just trimming cost.
Fertility clinics are deploying AI for sperm and embryo selection, but experts are split on whether it raises live-birth rates. Limited clinical validation and ethical questions dominate the debate.

Early evidence suggests AI-driven 'deskilling' is already measurable in medicine and software engineering. The piece reviews studies where professionals leaning on AI tools lose independent proficiency.

A mechanistic modeling framework augmented with machine learning optimizes mRNA process parameters and enables quality-by-design manufacturing. The modular approach links unit operations so models transfer across processes.

Machine learning applied to cell and gene therapy manufacturing promises predictive control and real-time anomaly detection. Proponents argue it could turn a batch-art process into a measurable, closed-loop one.

A preprint shows biological continued pretraining reshapes a foundation model's capability profile without catastrophic forgetting — 'biological CPT does not degrade the model; it lifts it' across knowledge, code and biomedical benchmarks. Evidence that domain science data can improve general models rather than narrow them.

EcoXAI is an autonomous agentic ecosystem for explainable AI in biomedical discovery, grounding multi-agent analysis in established biological knowledge. It targets the interpretability gap that blocks AI findings from entering the literature.

MolMAE is a surface-centric multimodal masked autoencoder for molecular representation learning. It fuses molecular surface, graph and sequence views to improve property prediction across diverse tasks.
